text: Seed `column_types` for lookup seeds go in `seeds/lookups/_lookups.yml`, one entry per non-text column.
Use sparklines sparingly; every chart must answer a stated question.
Name notebooks `YYYY-MM-DD_<author>_<topic>.ipynb`; a notebook reused twice is promoted to a script or model.
Feature tables for ML are `ft_<entity>_<window>`.
Vendor API clients live in `src/clients/` with one module per vendor.
Scripts run under `python -m` from the repo root; no `sys.path` edits.
Prefer vendors with SOC 2 Type II reports; store the latest report in the vault.
Write in present tense and active voice; avoid 'simply' and 'just'.
Use `count(*)` for rows and `count(col)` only when you want non-null counts.
Run `sqlfluff lint` only on changed `.sql` files in PRs, all files on main.
Cluster keys are added only after `SYSTEM$CLUSTERING_INFORMATION` shows poor depth.
Use `git commit --fixup` while addressing review so reviewers can follow changes.
Avoid `SELECT *` on wide tables; BigQuery bills for scanned columns.
Quality results are written to `ops.dq_results` and graphed on the data health dashboard.
Slot reservations are assigned per project; the `etl` project gets baseline 500 slots.
Wrap every timestamp column in `{{ to_utc('col') }}` and alias it with an `_at` suffix; plain `date` columns are left alone.
Promote a build from the staging environment to prod only after approval in #data-release.
`BigQueryInsertJobOperator` tasks set an explicit `execution_timeout`; the default of none hangs the scheduler queue.
BI Engine reservations are sized by the BI team and reviewed quarterly.
A new staging source must be in the sources yml; the model yml lists only final-select columns, by aliased name.
Review slot usage for `marts` jobs monthly and tag outliers in #data-cost.
Multi-cluster warehouses cap `MAX_CLUSTER_COUNT` at 3 unless approved in #data-cost.
Never delete evidence: snapshot logs and query history before cleaning up.
Entity names are singular and match the mart's primary key concept.
Shadow-deploy a new model for a week before switching traffic.
A lookup seed that changes more than once a month should become a managed table with an admin UI.
Don't use `SERIAL` for new tables; use identity columns.
Notebook parameters (dates, schema names) go in the first code cell, tagged `parameters`.
Set `temperature=0` for extraction and classification tasks.
Stop the bleeding first: pause the DAG or revert the deploy before diagnosing.
Tag every warehouse and project with `cost_center`; untagged spend is billed to platform.
Convert integer `*_cents` columns with `{{ cents_to_dollars('x_cents') }}` and drop the suffix (`amount`); no `*_cents` in staging output.
Explores define `sql_always_where` for tenant filtering where relevant.
Unit tests run in under 30 seconds in total; slower tests are marked `integration`.
Datasets are regional; keep `analytics` and `raw_events` in the same region to avoid cross-region copies.
Teardown must run even when a test fails; use fixtures with `yield`.
Terraform plans run in CI on every PR touching `terraform/`; apply only from main.
Dataset-triggered DAGs are preferred over cron offsets for downstream dependencies.
Test a macro on both Snowflake and BigQuery before merging when it uses date functions.
`TRANSFORM_WH` has a dedicated resource monitor and an owner listed in `snowflake/warehouses.yml`.
If the source has `_is_deleted`, add `where not _is_deleted` in the renamed CTE and do not select the column.
Right-size Airflow workers quarterly using utilization graphs.
Each script's docstring states inputs, outputs, and who to ask.
Lookup seeds are loaded with `dbt seed --select tag:lookup` before any model build in CI.
A column rename in a published data contract is a major version bump with 30 days of dual publishing.
Name resources with the module's `name_prefix` input for consistent naming.
Feature tables are versioned by suffix; consumers pin a version and migrate deliberately.
Do not rewrite history on shared release branches.
Add a `-- example:` line in the macro header with a rendered call.
Seed CSVs use lower_snake_case headers and end with a trailing newline, and an existing seed is never reformatted inside a feature PR.
